instructions: If you have time, season the roast up to 1 hour before you cook: sprinkle 1 1/4 tsp of the salt and 3/4 tsp of the pepper all over it and leave it on a plate on the counter.

Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Meanwhile, coarsely chop the onion and the 3 garlic cloves. Peel the 4 carrots and cut them into 2 inch pieces, halve the 1 lb potatoes, and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.

Pat the roast dry with paper towels. Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium high until it shimmers. Add the roast and leave it alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pot. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.
Turn the roast and brown each of the other sides the same way, about 12 to 15 minutes in all. Move it to a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the onion. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Stir in the 2 tbsp tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it turns a shade darker.
Pour in the 3/4 cup wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, until it has cooked down by about a quarter.

Add the 3 cups broth, the 2 bay leaves, 4 sprigs of the thyme, the chopped parsley and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Put the roast back in with any juices from the plate and bring it to a simmer.
Put the lid on and move the pot to the oven. Cook for 2 hours.

Take the pot out and tuck the carrots and potatoes around the roast, pushing them down into the liquid. Put the lid back on and cook for 1 hour more, until the roast pulls apart easily with two forks and the vegetables are tender. If the meat still feels tough, give it another 30 minutes.
Lift the roast and vegetables onto a platter and cover them loosely with foil. Fish the bay leaves and thyme stems out of the pot.

Stir the 1 1/2 tbsp cornstarch with 1 1/2 tbsp cold water in a small cup until smooth. Set the pot over medium heat on the stove and bring the liquid to a simmer. Stir in the cornstarch mix and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Taste the gravy. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Pull the roast into big pieces with two forks. Chop 2 tbsp more of the parsley and scatter it over the top. Serve with the vegetables and the gravy.
method_notes: Both versions salt a chuck roast, sear it hard in a Dutch oven, soften onion and garlic in the same pot, cook tomato paste into it, deglaze with a cup of red wine and braise the roast in beef stock with thyme until it pulls apart. Natasha's Kitchen lets the salted roast sit for an hour, braises at 325°F for 3 to 4 hours with bay leaves, parsley and carrots in from the start, and thickens the liquid with cornstarch at the end. The Modern Proper uses 350°F, adds a spoonful of brown sugar and puts carrots and baby potatoes in for the last hour. This follows Natasha's Kitchen for a 3 lb roast for 4, with the potatoes and the later vegetable timing from The Modern Proper so they stay whole.
